A short profile of the anechoic chamber at Aalto University’s acoustics lab on the Otaniemi campus in Espoo, the largest anechoic chamber in Finland. The chamber is a 500-tonne block lined with foam wedges that absorb sound and suppress reflections, and it rests on springs so that ground vibration cannot reach it.

Researchers use it to study loudspeaker technology and how people perceive low frequencies. Because there is no reverberation, they can measure exactly what a sound source emits. The background noise level is −2 dB, below the threshold of human hearing, and it is said that inside you can hear the blood flowing through your veins.

Source: Aalto University; shared by Fanyu Meng on Ziyu Acoustics.
